q: 255. The cement mortar mix generally used for internal plaster
explain: For internal plastering, a 1:4 mix (one part cement to four parts sand) is standard as it provides a good balance of workability and strength without excessive shrinkage.

q: 256. The cement mortar mix generally used for external plaster
explain: External plaster requires high resistance to weathering; a 1:4 mix is typically used to ensure durability and water-tightness.

q: 257. The cement mortar mix generally used for ceiling plaster
explain: Ceiling plaster needs a richer mix (1:3) to provide better adhesion and to counteract the effects of gravity during application.

q: 258. During Rana Cracy, types of mortar generally used for public buildings are
explain: Historically in Nepal (Rana Era), lime and surkhi (crushed brick) were the primary binding materials before cement became widely available.

q: 259. The property of steel enabling it to be drawn into thin wires is called
explain: Ductility is the physical property of a material associated with the ability to be hammered thin or stretched into wire without breaking.

q: 260. The Property of metals because of which they can be transformed into different shapes by heating is called
explain: Malleability is the ability of a metal to be deformed under compression, often improved by heating, allowing it to be rolled or hammered into sheets.

q: 261. The property due to which steel can withstand hammer blows is called
explain: Toughness is the ability of a material to absorb energy and deform plastically without fracturing, essential for resisting impact or hammer blows.

q: 262. The operation of removal of impurities or clay adhering to iron ores is known as
explain: Dressing involves the mechanical removal of impurities like clay and stones from the ore before chemical processing.

q: 263. Pig iron made from haematite are free from sulphur, phosphorus and copper is known as
explain: Bessemer pig iron is high-quality pig iron low in phosphorus and sulphur, specifically suitable for the Bessemer steel-making process.

q: 264. The pig iron obtained from the furnace that is property provided with fuel at very high temperature is called
explain: Foundry pig iron is produced under conditions that allow it to be easily remelted and cast into various shapes.

q: 265. The pig iron obtained from the furnace that is property provided with insufficient fuel at very low temperature is called
explain: Forge pig iron is produced at lower temperatures and is generally used for making wrought iron.

q: 266. The process involved in the manufacture of wrought iron from pig iron is known as
explain: Wrought iron manufacture involves refining the pig iron, 'puddling' to remove carbon, and rolling to create the fibrous structure.

q: 267. For melting one tonne of cast iron the requirement of material is
explain: The melting process in a cupola furnace requires specific ratios of fuel (coke), flux (limestone), and air for combustion.

q: 268. Pig iron contains carbon up to
explain: Pig iron is the immediate product of smelting iron ore and has a very high carbon content, typically between 3% and 5%.

q: 269. The property of steel is influenced maximum by
explain: Carbon content is the primary factor that determines the hardness, strength, and ductility of steel.

q: 270. Purest form of iron is
explain: Wrought iron contains less than 0.15% carbon and very few impurities, making it the purest commercial form of iron.

q: 271. As compared to mild steel, cast iron has
explain: Cast iron is brittle; it is very strong in compression but fails easily under tension compared to the ductile mild steel.

q: 272. Wrought iron contains carbon up to
explain: To maintain its purity and fibrous nature, wrought iron carbon content is strictly limited, usually below 0.15%.

q: 273. Mild steel contains carbon up to
explain: Mild steel (low carbon steel) typically has a carbon range of 0.15% to 0.25%.

q: 274. The unit weight of steel in taken as
explain: The standard density of steel used in engineering calculations is approximately 7850 kg/m3 or 7.85 ton/m3.

q: 275. Vanadium steel in generally used for
explain: Vanadium increases the fatigue strength and toughness of steel, making it ideal for high-stress automotive parts like axles and springs.

q: 276. Cast iron is used for
explain: Because cast iron is excellent in compression, it was historically used for vertical members like columns and struts.

q: 277. Mild steel is used for
explain: Mild steel's high tensile strength and ductility make it the standard material for structural beams and reinforcement.

q: 278. Wrought iron is used for
explain: Wrought iron's corrosion resistance made it a popular choice for water pipes and decorative ironwork before the advent of galvanized steel.

q: 279. The types of steel used for precision leveling staff in
explain: Invar has an extremely low coefficient of thermal expansion, ensuring that precision leveling staffs do not change length with temperature.

q: 280. The steel used for rails under heavy traffic and sharp curves in
explain: Manganese steel (Hadfield steel) is 'work-hardening,' meaning it gets harder as it is impacted, making it perfect for heavy-duty rails.

q: 281. The steel used for manufacture of rails in
explain: Bessemer steel was historically the primary material for rails because the process allowed for the economical production of large quantities of steel with the necessary hardness.

q: 282. Softer variety of steel may be obtained by
explain: The crucible process allows for high control over the composition, often used to produce high-quality, uniform tool steel or softer, specialized varieties.

q: 283. Brass is an alloy of
explain: Brass is a non-ferrous alloy primarily consisting of copper and zinc. The proportions can be varied to achieve different mechanical and electrical properties.

q: 284. Bronze is as alloy of
explain: Bronze is an alloy consisting primarily of copper, usually with tin as the main additive, making it harder and more durable than pure copper.

q: 285. Invar is an alloy of
explain: Invar (FeNi36) is a nickel-iron alloy notable for its uniquely low coefficient of thermal expansion, making it essential for precision instruments.

q: 286. Solder is an alloy of
explain: Soft solder is typically an alloy of lead and tin, characterized by a low melting point used to join metal workpieces.

q: 287. German silver is an alloy of
explain: Despite its name, German silver contains no actual silver; it is composed of copper, nickel, and zinc, resembling silver in appearance.

q: 288. Monel metal is an alloy of
explain: Monel is a group of nickel alloys, primarily composed of nickel (up to 67%) and copper, with small amounts of iron, manganese, carbon, and silicon.

q: 289. Stainless steel resists corrosion due to
explain: Chromium reacts with oxygen to form a thin, invisible, and self-healing layer of chromium oxide, which protects the steel from rusting.

q: 290. For the manufacture of stainless steel, steel is mixed width
explain: Chromium is the essential alloying element (at least 10.5%) that transforms steel into stainless steel.

q: 291. Galvanizing means
options: depositing a fine film of zinc on iron/steel by dipping it in molten zinc
explain: Galvanization is the process of applying a protective zinc coating to steel or iron to prevent rusting.

q: 292. A combination of metals with other substances is called
explain: An alloy is a metallic substance composed of two or more elements, as either a compound or a solution.

q: 293. The main purpose of manufacture of alloys steel is to attain a certain properties like
explain: Alloying elements are added to steel to improve various characteristics, including mechanical strength, hardness, and impact resistance (toughness).

q: 294. The artificial seasoning of timber may
explain: Seasoning is the process of removing the sap or moisture from timber to prevent decay and improve its stability for construction.

q: 295. Which one of the following does not belong to endogenous trees?
explain: Endogenous trees grow inwards (like bamboo or palm). Teak is an exogenous tree, meaning it grows outwards by adding annual rings.

q: 296. Which one of the following does not belong to exogenous trees?
explain: Coconut is an endogenous tree; its fibers are distributed throughout the stem rather than growing in concentric rings.

q: 297. The solution of salts from the soil absorbed by the trees which becomes a viscous solution due to loss of moisture and action of carbon dioxide is known as
explain: As per Key b but Sap is the fluid that circulates through a plant's vascular system, carrying nutrients and water.

q: 298. The age of tree can be judged from
explain: In exogenous trees, one annual ring is typically added each year. Counting these rings in a cross-section reveals the tree's age.

q: 299. The no. of annual ring in a log of 30 then life of the timber is
explain: Since one annual ring generally represents one year of growth, 30 rings indicate a tree life of 30 years.

q: 300. The layer between the bark of the tree and the sap wood which is not yet converted into wood is called
explain: The cambium layer is the thin layer of living cells between the inner bark and the sapwood where new wood and bark cells are produced.

q: 301. Which of the following is not a hard wood?
explain: Deodar is a coniferous tree (softwood), whereas Sal, Teak, and Oak are deciduous (hardwood).

q: 302. Which of the following is not a soft wood?
explain: Sisham (Rosewood) is a dense hardwood. Deodar and Kail are common softwoods.

q: 303. When the timber is attacked by fungus and reduced to powder, it is called
explain: Dry rot is a form of decay caused by specific fungi that digest the cellulose of the wood, leaving it brittle and powdery.

q: 304. In dry rot, wooden material defect caused due to
explain: Dry rot is exclusively a fungal disease that spreads in timber with poor ventilation and moderate moisture.

q: 305. Which of the following wood has the maximum resistance to white ants?
explain: Teak contains natural oils and silica that make it highly resistant to termites (white ants) and decay.

q: 306. Creosote oil is used to preserve the wood from
explain: Creosote is a powerful wood preservative that prevents fungal rot and deters wood-boring insects and termites.

q: 307. Timber can be made reasonably fire resistant
options: by soaking it in ammonium sulphate
by pumping creosote oil into timber under high pressure
explain: Ammonium sulphate or borax are fire-retardant chemicals that release non-combustible gases when heated, protecting the timber.

q: 308. The main purpose of seasoning is
options: to make the timber fire resistant
to remove the moisture from the timber at uniform rate
to make the timber water proof
explain: Seasoning aims to reduce the moisture content (sap) of timber to equilibrium with the surroundings to prevent warping and shrinkage.

q: 309. Which one is false?
options: seasoning is done to control moisture
sal wood is used for ornamental purpose
sap is suck in spring by roots of the tree
explain: Sal wood is very hard and durable, making it excellent for structural beams and door frames, but it is too coarse for fine ornamental/furniture work.

q: 310. The seasoning of timber
options: makes the timber light, strong and stable
prevents warping, cracking and shrinkage in timber
makes timber resistant to decay by fungi, termites etc.
explain: Properly seasoned timber is more durable, easier to work with, and less prone to biological attacks or structural deformation.

q: 311. Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: kiln seasoned timber is stronger than natural seasoned timber
moisture content in the timber can be reduced to any desired level in kiln seasoning
kiln seasoning is quicker than natural seasoning
kiln seasoning requires less stacking space but more expensive
explain: Kiln seasoning is faster and more controlled, but it doesn't necessarily make timber 'stronger' than natural air seasoning; if done too fast, it can actually cause internal stress.

q: 312. In a well-seasoned timber, the moisture content will be in the range of
explain: For most construction purposes, timber is considered well-seasoned when its moisture content is reduced to roughly 10-12%.

q: 313. Most economical methods of sawing wood is
explain: Flat (or plain) sawing is the quickest and most economical method with minimal waste, although it is more prone to warping.

q: 314. A thin sheet of wood sliced from a log of wood is called
explain: Veneers are thin slices of wood, usually thinner than 3mm, used to cover cheaper wood surfaces or glued together to make plywood.

q: 315. The number of veneers glued under pressure in a plywood must be
explain: Plywood layers (plies) are always an odd number to ensure structural balance and prevent the board from warping or curling.

q: 316. The curved swellings from the growth of layers or wounds left after branches are cut off in an irregular manners, are known as
explain: Rind galls are curved swellings that form over a wound on the tree, often where a branch has been improperly removed.

q: 317. The defects in wood due to hardening is
explain: as per key c but The options listed (knots, rind galls, burls) are growth defects. Hardening usually refers to 'case hardening' during improper seasoning, which is not listed.

q: 318. The defect caused by the shrinkage of timber is
explain: A crook is a warp along the edge of a board, typically caused by uneven shrinkage during the drying process.

q: 319. Knots in timber are
explain: Knots are the bases of branches that have been encased by the subsequent growth of the wood in the main trunk.

q: 320. Impregnating of timber is done to increase
explain: Impregnating timber with chemicals (like Abel's process) is primarily done to improve its resistance to fire or biological decay.

q: 321. Based on its dry weight, a freshly felled tree may contain water
explain: Freshly cut timber (green timber) can often have a moisture content of 100% or more relative to its oven-dry weight.

q: 322. The time required for the seasoning of timber in air is about
explain: As per key c but While it varies by species and thickness, initial air seasoning of thin softwoods can take as little as 1 to 2 months to reach a workable state.

q: 323. In the manufacture of ply woods the veneers are placed such that the grains of one layer are
options: at 45° with the grains of the other
at right angles with the grains of the other
at 60° with the grains of the other
parallel to the grains of the other
explain: Cross-lamination (placing grains at 90°) gives plywood uniform strength in both directions and reduces shrinkage/expansion.

q: 324. Plywood is identified by
explain: Commercial plywood is primarily categorized and sold based on its thickness (e.g., 4mm, 6mm, 12mm).

q: 325. Plywood is obtained by gluing wooden sheets at a specification of
explain: The manufacture of plywood requires both high mechanical pressure and specific heat to cure the adhesive bonds between veneers.

q: 326. Plywood is generally available
explain: While available in many sizes, 3-ply boards typically start around the 3 to 4 mm thickness range.

q: 327. Which has great strength against the rut?
explain: Teak is renowned for its extreme durability and resistance to rot and fungal attacks due to its natural oils.

q: 328. The wood of which tree is used to make cricket bat
explain: Willow wood is used because it is incredibly light, tough, and has high shock resistance (impact energy absorption).

q: 329. The seasoning of timber is done for
explain: Seasoning involves controlling the drying process to reach an equilibrium moisture content relative to the surrounding humidity.

q: 330. The strength of timber is maximum along
explain: Timber is an anisotropic material; its tensile and compressive strength are significantly higher when loaded parallel to the fibers (grains).

q: 331. Seasoning of timber is done to
options: reduce the weight of the timber
explain: Removing moisture makes the timber lighter for transport, stable against further shrinkage, and less susceptible to rot.

q: 332. The defects in the growth of timber are called
explain: Shakes (separations between rings) and checks (cracks across rings) are common structural defects occurring during growth or seasoning.

q: 333. The trunk of tree left after cutting all the branches is known as
explain: A 'log' is the raw trunk of a tree that has been felled and delimbed but not yet sawn into lumber.

q: 334. A piece of sawn timber whose c/s dimensions exceed 5 cm, in one direction and 20 cm in the other direction, is called a
explain: A baulk is a roughly squared timber piece of large cross-section, usually exceeding 50mm in thickness and 200mm in width.

q: 335. A piece of timber whose thickness and width are respectively 5 cm and 10 cm is called
explain: A 'deal' is a specific commercial size of sawn softwood, typically between 5-10cm thick and 20-25cm wide.

q: 336. The chemical used in preserving timber are
explain: Zinc chloride, coal tar, and creosote are all well-known chemical preservatives used to protect wood from moisture and pests.

q: 337. The trees yielding hard wood is
explain: Shisham is a broad-leaved exogenous tree (hardwood). Chir, Deodar, and Pine are conifers (softwoods).

q: 338. The trees yielding soft wood is
explain: Chir and Deodar are conifers, which produce softwood. Sal, Teak, and Shisham are hardwoods.

q: 339. According to IS:399-1963, the weight of the timber is specified at
explain: Standard engineering codes usually specify timber properties and density at a standard moisture content of 12%.

q: 340. Ply wood is made from
explain: Plywood is typically manufactured using veneers from common available timbers like mango, teak, or pine, depending on the required grade.

q: 341. The sports goods are made from
explain: Mulberry is highly valued for sports goods (like hockey sticks) due to its toughness and flexibility.

q: 342. The timber used for decorative wood work
explain: As per key c but Shisham, Siris, and Rosewood all have beautiful grain patterns and colors, making them ideal for high-end furniture and decorative carving.

q: 343. The unit weight of sal is
explain: As per key c but Sal is a very dense and heavy hardwood, with a unit weight typically around 880 to 950 kg/m3.

q: 344. Normally the wood used for scaffolding is
explain: Bamboo is the standard for scaffolding due to its high strength-to-weight ratio, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness.

q: 345. The ingredient which gives the desired colour to a paint is called
explain: Pigments are finely ground solid particles that provide color, opacity, and some level of protection in paint.

q: 346. The paints with white lead base are suitable for painting of
explain: White lead base is excellent for wood because it is very durable and flexible, but it is rarely used on iron as it can promote corrosion compared to red lead.

q: 347. The function of base of an oil paint is
options: to form the body of the paint
to reinforce the film of the paint after drying
to prevent penetration of paint to lower surfaces
explain: The 'base' (like white lead or zinc oxide) provides the bulk or body of the paint and determines its character.

q: 348. The vehicle used in case of enamel paints is
explain: As per key but Enamel paint is essentially a mixture of pigment and varnish, which gives it a hard, glossy finish.

q: 349. The main component of oil paint is
explain: Oil paint requires a base/pigment, a vehicle (carrier), and a thinner (like turpentine) to be effective.

q: 350. The pigment in paints gives
explain: The primary role of the pigment is to provide color and hide the surface being painted.
